doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

chapter: Coming up on the L.A. scene
title: Meeting Bobby Hutcherson and playing fast bebop
summary: The unwritten audition was fast bebop; Goodwin describes first playing with Hutcherson, Terry Trotter and Herbie Lewis and having no technique but playing the music.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Was there an audition piece — I remember in the early ‘60s if a drummer could play “Wipe Out” you know like okay you can be in our garage band. Was there something similar to that back then that you would be expected to be able to do?

Yeah. I first met Bobby Hutcherson when Terry Trotter, the pianist, took me over to Bobby’s house to play with Bobby and him and Herbie Lewis the bass player. And they were a year older than me. And the first thing Bobby said to me after, “Do you have any marijuana” was, “Can you play fast?” I said, “I don’t know, let’s find out.” So they put “From This Moment on” way, way up. And, you know, I guess I did okay. I really didn’t © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

know how to play the drums. I had no technique at all, but I could hear and I could follow music and I could play music in other words, I just didn’t have a solid technique on the drums or any technique on the drums.

It’s very fortuitous that you just said, “I could play music” because in this particular record in the fine print inside, Phil Woods says, “Bill Goodwin plays the music.” He didn’t say he plays the drums, he said you play the music.

I always play the song and I know, most of the songs I play I know them well, I know the lyrics, I know something about the origin and all that, and I love — you know like I love books and music and I like knowing things about them.
